LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 11.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 11 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we look at the face of people as they speak? 2) How are audio stories different from a written story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to audio stories and pick put specific sounds, words, phrases or sentences,

2. say words with the sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ correctly,

3. say tongue twisters with the target sounds,

4. collaborate to listen to choral poems with the sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ and pick out words with the selected sounds,

5. interpret non-verbal cues correctly during conversations,

6. practise using expressions such as fixed phrases: out of breath; 1)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to audio stories and pick put specific sounds, words, phrases or sentences,
2. say words with the sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ correctly,
3. say tongue twisters with the target sounds,
4. collaborate to listen to choral poems with the sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ and pick out words with the selected sounds,
5. interpret non-verbal cues correctly during conversations,
6. practise using expressions such as fixed phrases: out of breath; 1)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to speak fluently and clearly is enhanced as they say tongue twisters that

contain the target sounds.

• Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to manipulate digital devices is developed while listening to audio stories

and picking out specific sounds, words, phrases or sentences.

Values:
• Unity: This is cultivated as the learner collaborates with peers by listening to choral poems and picking out words

with the selected sounds.

• Social justice: It is displayed by the learner as they foster fairness while working with peers to listen to choral

poems.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills (Effective communication): The learner’s clarity in communication is developed as they engage in role- play and retell the events in the story.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the correct use of words and expressions to the completing of written assignments

correctly in Religious Education.
